llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions broadly match its stated purpose (sync WhatsApp/Telegram → Obsidian with local Ollama search and optional Git backup), but there are several mismatches and operational risks—most notably a gap between the claimed automatic privacy/redaction guarantees and the actual code (no sanitizer is present), a hard-coded default Ollama endpoint, and automatic Git push behavior that could leak data if misconfigured.

dimensions.detail: The repo, SKILL.md, and _meta.json consistently describe WhatsApp/Telegram → Obsidian ingestion, Ollama local embedding/search, and Git backup. Declared tool permissions (read/write/exec/memory_search) are consistent with that functionality. However, the skill claims automatic '隐私脱敏' (redaction) and safe GitHub backup while the shipped scripts (push/sync) perform raw git commits/pushes and there is no concrete code in the repo that performs the described automatic sanitization prior to commit—this is an implementation gap.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and prompts require reading Obsidian note files and running git push scripts. The SKILL.md and prompts state that sensitive items (API keys, tokens, passwords, phone numbers, emails) will be automatically replaced, but no script in the repo performs regex redaction or content sanitization before committing; the only actionable scripts simply add, commit and push. That means the claimed privacy protections rely on the agent’s prompt-driven processing being executed correctly before the push; if that step is missed or bypassed, secrets could be committed and pushed. The prompt also specifies token-detection heuristics (ghp_, sk-, etc.)—this is good, but it's only in prompt text, not enforced in code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) and included scripts are small shell/Python files; no external downloads, package installs, or archive extracts are present. This minimizes install-time supply-chain risk. The only notable artifact is a default local IP used by the search script (see environment_proportionality).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, yet the Python search uses OLLAMA_BASE_URL and OLLAMA_MODEL environment variables and defaults OLLAMA_BASE_URL to http://192.168.3.120:11434. A hard-coded private IP as a default endpoint is unusual and could cause unintended network calls if the user does not explicitly set OLLAMA_BASE_URL to a known local instance. The scripts expect git credentials/configured remotes to be present (SSH keys or stored credentials) but the skill does not explicitly request or document credential handling—this is expected for git backup but increases the risk of accidental push to an incorrectly configured remote. The number of environment/credential accesses is not excessive, but defaults and implicit network endpoints create risk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always:true and is user-invocable. _meta.json declares file_read/file_write/exec permissions which are consistent with reading local Obsidian notes, writing new markdown files, running git, and calling a local Ollama server. Those privileges are required for the stated functionality, but they are powerful: with autonomous agents or scheduled agents (promised '整理专家'/'复盘专家'), the skill can periodically commit and push contents. Combined with the earlier absence of enforced sanitization, periodic autonomous pushes increase the blast radius if misconfigured.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Summary of what to check before installing:

1) Privacy redaction is described in prompts but not implemented in the push scripts—verify that you run the agent-level sanitization step (or add explicit sanitization) before any git commit. Do not assume redaction is automatic just because the README/prompts say so.
2) Configure OLLAMA_BASE_URL explicitly to your known local Ollama instance; the search script defaults to http://192.168.3.120:11434 which is a hard-coded private IP. If left unchanged it will attempt network requests to that address.
3) Inspect and control your git remote: the push/sync scripts will commit and push whatever is in the configured Obsidian directory. Ensure the remote is a private repo you control, and test the workflow in an isolated environment first (or disable automatic pushes until you confirm redaction works).
4) Ensure git credentials (SSH keys or access tokens) are stored safely and that the agent cannot push to unintended remotes. Consider requiring manual approval before push or modifying the scripts to require an explicit environment flag to enable pushing.
5) If you expect the skill to guarantee no secret leaks, add an explicit code-level sanitizer that scans files for tokens/patterns and blocks or redacts commits, rather than relying solely on prompt-instructions.

Given these gaps, treat this skill as useful but operationally risky until you verify sanitization and network/remote settings. If you want, I can suggest small code changes to add enforced redaction before commit and to make the Ollama endpoint/configuration safer.
